# TREX documentation

> TREX 1.0.0 estimates conditional false-positive probabilities for TESS
> transit signals. It does not validate or confirm planets.

Resolve these links relative to this file to stay on the same release.

## Start here

- [Overview](README.md): purpose and common tasks
- [Installation](installation.md): Python 3.14, platform requirements and CUDA
- [Tutorial](tutorial.md): offline synthetic run, then a measured-signal workflow
- [From a TIC ID](from-tic.md): scene acquisition and its limits
- [Prepared runs](prepared-runs.md): single-curve and joint observations
- [Outputs](outputs.md): summary.json, scenarios.csv, failure.json and interpretation

## Reference and explanation

- [Full index](index.md): all pages, including the glossary and troubleshooting
- [Inputs](inputs.md): photometry, stellar scene, background population and units
- [Python API](api.md): scene, target, inference, AstroImageJ and Gaia inputs
- [From a scene](from-scene.md): offline scene and contrast-curve path
- [Concepts](concepts.md): transits, false positives, scenarios, FPP/NFPP and ESS
- [How TREX works](how-trex-works.md): priors, forward model, evidence and limits
- [Relationship to TRICERATOPS](differences-from-triceratops.md): provenance and source-level differences

## Measurement records

- [Synthetic quick-start, CPU completion](measurements/quickstart-cpu-2026-11-10.md): one full-budget synthetic run and its limits
- [Earlier CPU pause](measurements/quickstart-cpu-2026-11-09.md): superseded historical record
